headline: Bench Khalil Shakir for MarShawn Lloyd at FLEX before tonight's 5:15 PM PT kickoff — his snaps have fallen to 62.5% while Lloyd is Green Bay's clear feature back.
summary: Danny is 1-0 with a favorable Sunday slate ahead. Two FLEX upgrades are sitting on the bench: Lloyd over a diminished Shakir (act tonight) and Jones over Judkins (act by Sunday). Burrow and Johnson are both Questionable but expected to play; Burrow needs an auto-sub set since none is recorded.

lineup.why: Shakir's snap share fell to 62.5% in Week 1 (down from ~75% the past two years) on a thin 5.8-target projection, while Lloyd is Green Bay's confirmed feature back with Josh Jacobs still on the exempt list.
lineup.evidence: Sept 16 reports: Shakir played 62.5% of Buffalo's dropbacks in Week 1, caught 4 of 6 targets as the clear third read behind DJ Moore and Dalton Kincaid, and analysts are recommending he be benched in Week 2. Lloyd is confirmed as the Packers' lead back (11.5 projected carries) with Jacobs still on the commissioner's exempt list and no return timetable.

lineup.why: Jordan Mason's move to IR hands Jones the full Vikings backfield lead in a much better game than Judkins' tough spot in Cleveland.
lineup.evidence: Sept 16: Vikings placed Jordan Mason on IR (thumb fracture, out 4+ weeks) and Jones is set for the bulk of backfield touches, in a game with a 22-point implied total. Judkins remains Cleveland's clear starter (24 touches Week 1) but the Browns are 8.5-point underdogs at Tampa Bay with only a 16.5 implied total behind a shaky offensive line.

subs.why: Burrow (Questionable, back) was limited at Wednesday's practice but is adamant he'll play; Willis's game kicks off later (1:25 PM PT) so he's full cover — set the pair before Burrow's Sunday 10:00 AM PT kickoff.

Johnson (Questionable, illness) was a DNP at Wednesday's practice with two more practice days to prove out; no bench TE is rostered, so watch Sunday's inactive report (posts ~90 minutes before the 10:00 AM PT kickoff) and be ready to bench him yourself.
